settlementFee.note: TITLE INSURANCE PREMIUMS in Florida are fixed by Fla. Stat. §627.782/§627.7825 and Florida Administrative Code 69O-186.003, and are UNIFORM across every title insurer/agent in the state at a given liability amount. This is not a provider-set price and is included here for regulatory context. Independently confirmed identical across two separately-sourced documents this session (flrules.elaws.us's rule summary and FNTI's own PDF republication of the FAC text, both showing the same per-thousand rates and minimums).
settlementFee.ownerLeaseholdAndMortgagePremium: $0-$100,000 of liability: $5.75 per thousand. $100,000-$1,000,000, add $5.00 per thousand. $1,000,000-$5,000,000, add $2.50 per thousand. $5,000,000-$10,000,000, add $2.25 per thousand. Over $10,000,000, add $2.00 per thousand.
settlementFee.minimumPremium: $100.00 for all conveyances except multiple conveyances; $60.00 for multiple conveyances on the same property
settlementFee.reissueRates: Up to $100,000: $3.30/thousand; $100,000-$1M add $3.00/thousand; $1M-$10M add $2.00/thousand; over $10M add $1.50/thousand. Minimum $100.00.
settlementFee.simultaneousIssueMortgagePolicy: Minimum $25.00 when not exceeding the owner's policy amount
settlementFee.minimumInsurerRetention: 30% of risk premium (35%-40% at higher liability tiers per the table above)
settlementFee.sampleCalculatedPremiums_fromProviderPag: Cross-checked against provider restatements of the same table this session: $100,000 liability = $575.00 (VyStar Title Agency); $150,000 = $825.00 and $200,000 = $1,075.00 (Palm Beach Title & Escrow); $500,000 = $2,575.00 and $1,000,000 = $5,075.00 (VyStar Title Agency) -- all consistent with the promulgated formula above, no discrepancies found across any of the 5+ independent provider restatements encountered this session.

other.name: Closing services fee bundling requirement (regulatory finding, not a fee itself)
other.amount: Per Fla. Stat./DFS guidance confirmed at myfloridacfo.com this session: the 'closing services fee' line on the settlement statement must include ALL fees and charges made by the title agency to close the transaction -- postage, notary services, copies, digital documents, document preparation, and storage fees may NOT be itemized as separate line items; they must be bundled into one figure. DFS explicitly does not regulate the AMOUNT of this fee, only its presentation.

bundlingNotes: FL is a promulgated-rate state: the premium is identical for every title insurer/agent in Florida at a given liability amount and effective date, confirmed by cross-checking the OIR rule text against five independent provider restatements of the same table (VyStar Title Agency, Palm Beach Title & Escrow, Atlantic Title Firm, Leading Edge Title of Central Florida, Location Title & Escrow) -- all numerically identical to the FAC 69O-186.003 formula, with zero discrepancies. Because the premium is fixed, it carries NO market signal about provider competitiveness -- the settlement/closing/escrow fee (documented in the entries below) is the only place FL title companies compete on price, and Florida's own DFS regulatory guidance confirms that Florida uniquely REQUIRES ancillary items (notary, postage, copies, doc prep, storage) to be bundled into one non-itemized 'closing services fee' line rather than broken out separately -- a structural difference from itemization-heavy states like TX, and the likely reason so many FL provider fee pages quote a single flat number rather than a granular itemized list.
transactionContext: Applies uniformly to Owner's, Leasehold, and Mortgage title insurance premiums statewide, all metros, all provider types (national-brand underwriters, independent agents, attorneys). Premium calculation depends only on policy liability/face amount, not purchase-vs-refinance transaction type.

provider: Leading Edge Title of Central Florida (independent, Winter Park / Winter Springs / Lake Mary, FL -- Orlando metro)
asOf: Retrieved 2026-07-22; no explicit effective date stated on the page (described as current pricing)

itemizedFees.searchExam: Search Fee (seller side): $75; Municipal Lien Search (seller side): $150

bundlingNotes: One of the more itemized FL fee sheets found this session (search fee and municipal lien search broken out separately from the settlement fee on the seller side, rather than bundled) -- notably different from the Miami-Dade convention (Full Service Title) of bundling search/exam into the flat fee. Buyer-financed settlement fee ($675) is more than double the buyer-cash settlement fee ($295), a large within-provider purchase-financing-type spread not seen at other FL providers in this survey.
